plugin.hkdf.title: HKDF (HMAC-based key derivation)
plugin.hkdf.preset.rfc5869-a2: RFC 5869 A.2: HKDF-SHA-256 with long inputs (82-byte OKM)
plugin.hkdf.preset.rfc5869-a3: RFC 5869 A.3: HKDF-SHA-256 with empty salt and info
plugin.hkdf.preset.tls13-c-hs-traffic: TLS 1.3: client handshake traffic secret "c hs traffic" (RFC 8448)
plugin.hkdf.param.macHint: The HMAC that Extract and Expand call; HashLen is its output length.
plugin.hkdf.param.modeHint: Full HKDF, only one of its two halves, or the TLS 1.3 HKDF-Expand-Label.
plugin.hkdf.param.ikmHint: Up to 128 bytes, e.g. a Diffie-Hellman shared secret. Used by Extract.
plugin.hkdf.param.saltHint: Up to 128 bytes, may be empty: then Extract uses HashLen zero bytes (RFC 5869 §2.2).
plugin.hkdf.param.prkHint: The input of the Expand modes: at least HashLen and at most 128 bytes.
plugin.hkdf.param.infoEncodingHint: Whether info is UTF-8 text or hex bytes.
plugin.hkdf.param.infoHint: Up to 128 bytes of context that binds the output to its purpose; may be empty.
plugin.hkdf.param.lengthHint: 1 to 255 bytes (lab limit; RFC 5869 allows up to 255 · HashLen).
plugin.hkdf.param.label: TLS 1.3 label
plugin.hkdf.param.labelHint: Without the prefix "tls13 ", e.g. "derived" or "c hs traffic"; up to 249 bytes.
plugin.hkdf.param.contextHint: Up to 255 bytes, usually a transcript hash; may be empty.
plugin.hkdf.op.expand: Expand: T(i) = HMAC(PRK, T(i−1) ‖ info ‖ i)
plugin.hkdf.node.label: "tls13 " ‖ label
plugin.hkdf.derivation.title: HKDF
plugin.hkdf.step.initial.hkdf: HKDF with {{mac}} works in two halves. Extract condenses the {{ikmBytes}} bytes of IKM with the salt into a pseudorandom key PRK of HashLen = {{hashLen}} bytes. Expand stretches PRK into {{length}} bytes of OKM, in N = {{blocks}} HMAC calls.
plugin.hkdf.step.initial.extract: HKDF-Extract with {{mac}}: the {{ikmBytes}} bytes of IKM may be unevenly random, e.g. a Diffie-Hellman shared secret. Extract condenses them with the salt into a pseudorandom key (PRK) of HashLen = {{hashLen}} bytes.
plugin.hkdf.step.initial.expand: HKDF-Expand with {{mac}}: the PRK of {{prkBytes}} bytes is already a strong key. Expand stretches it into {{length}} bytes of OKM in N = {{blocks}} HMAC calls of HashLen = {{hashLen}} bytes each.
plugin.hkdf.step.initial.expandLabel: HKDF-Expand-Label (TLS 1.3) with {{mac}}: first the label "{{label}}", the context and the length are packed into the HkdfLabel struct; it serves as info. Then Expand derives {{length}} bytes in N = {{blocks}} HMAC calls of HashLen = {{hashLen}} bytes each.
plugin.hkdf.step.hkdfLabel: HkdfLabel = {{bytes}}. Its fields: the length as uint16 ({{length}} = {{lengthHex}}), a length byte ({{labelLength}}) and "tls13 {{label}}", then a length byte ({{contextLength}}) and the context {{context}}. The prefix "tls13 " separates TLS 1.3 keys from those of any other protocol that uses HKDF.
plugin.hkdf.step.extract: PRK = {{mac}}(salt, IKM) = {{prk}}. The {{saltBytes}}-byte salt is the HMAC key, the {{ikmBytes}} bytes of IKM are the message. A salt makes the output independent of the IKM's structure, even if an attacker knows that structure.
plugin.hkdf.step.extractZeroSalt: The salt is empty, so Extract uses HashLen = {{hashLen}} zero bytes as the HMAC key (RFC 5869 §2.2). PRK = {{mac}}(00…00, IKM) = {{prk}} from {{ikmBytes}} bytes of IKM.
plugin.hkdf.step.expandFirst: Block {{n}}: T({{n}}) = {{mac}}(PRK, info ‖ {{counter}}) = {{t}}. T(0) is empty, so the first HMAC input is just info and the counter byte {{counter}}.
plugin.hkdf.step.expand: Block {{n}}: T({{n}}) = {{mac}}(PRK, T({{prev}}) ‖ info ‖ {{counter}}) = {{t}}. Each block feeds the previous one back in, and the counter byte makes every HMAC input distinct.
plugin.hkdf.step.output: OKM = T(1) ‖ … ‖ T({{blocks}}) = {{okm}}: exactly the {{length}} requested bytes.
plugin.hkdf.step.outputTruncated: OKM = the first {{length}} bytes of T(1) ‖ … ‖ T({{blocks}}) = {{okm}}. The last {{dropped}} bytes of T({{blocks}}) are discarded.
plugin.hkdf.error.invalidParams: Give IKM, salt, PRK and context as hex text, and info, length and label as text.
plugin.hkdf.error.mode: Choose HKDF, Extract, Expand or Expand-Label.
plugin.hkdf.error.infoEncoding: Choose text or hex for info.
plugin.hkdf.error.ikmLength: IKM has {{length}} bytes; at most 128 are allowed.
plugin.hkdf.error.saltLength: The salt has {{length}} bytes; at most 128 are allowed.
plugin.hkdf.error.prkLength: PRK has {{length}} bytes; at most 128 are allowed.
plugin.hkdf.error.contextLength: The context has {{length}} bytes; at most 255 are allowed.
plugin.hkdf.error.infoLength: Info has {{length}} bytes; at most 128 are allowed.
plugin.hkdf.error.length: Give the output length L as a whole number from 1 to 255.
plugin.hkdf.error.labelLength: The label has {{length}} bytes; at most 249 are allowed, so that "tls13 " plus the label fit into 255.
plugin.hkdf.error.labelEmpty: HKDF-Expand-Label needs a label (TLS 1.3 labels have at least one byte after "tls13 ").
plugin.hkdf.error.notHmac: {{id}} is not an HMAC; HKDF is defined over HMAC.
plugin.hkdf.error.prkTooShort: PRK has {{length}} bytes; Expand needs at least HashLen = {{hashLen}} (RFC 5869 §2.3).
plugin.hkdf.error.lengthTooLong: L may be at most 255 · HashLen = {{max}} bytes, because the counter is a single byte.
